runner_ceilings_note: grok bills the WHOLE request at double rate past 200K prompt tokens, so this lane's ceiling cannot follow it there. The cap is a fact about the EXECUTOR, not the job, which is why it lives here rather than in ceiling_tokens — and why the lane keeps its own number for every other runner. Honored by both resolvers (ceiling_for and _budget_for) and cross-checked, so it is a bound rather than a comment. preplan reached the same conclusion by hand ('ceiling sits under the cliff on purpose in case this lane is ever routed to grok'); this generalises it to every lane that is over the cliff, which since the ladder is stage-agnostic is every lane that could ever fail over. ⚠️ CUMULATIVE, NOT PER-REQUEST — the label matters more than the number. xAI's 200K is a threshold on ONE request's prompt tokens; the resolver compares it against this manifest's declared unit, which is per-call CUMULATIVE context (input_toks + cache_read, the session's total across the tool loop). A 25-turn grok session averaging 60K per request reads 1.5M cumulative and breaches this bound with ZERO requests over the cliff. It is therefore a CONSERVATIVE cap: it binds in the safe direction, because a session containing a real crossing always exceeds it, but a breach here means 'over the conservative bound', NOT 'a confirmed doubled bill'. Reading it as the latter would cite an arithmetic artefact as a finding. True per-request cliff detection needs prompt tokens per request, which the fleet captures from no runner today — instrumentation, not a recompute.
